title: Moonshot AI Confidentially Files for Hong Kong IPO Targeting $3 Billion at ~$50 Billion Valuation
detail: Beijing-based Moonshot AI, developer of the Kimi chatbot and Kimi K3 model, confidentially submitted an A1 application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on September 3, according to people familiar with the plans, seeking to raise roughly $3 billion. The filing values the company at approximately $50 billion in its ongoing funding round — more than double the $20 billion valuation of its May 2026 raise led by Meituan. Kimi K3, launched in July 2026 with 2.8 trillion parameters, is billed by Moonshot as the largest open-weight model in the world. Founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, Moonshot said it had no comment on the report and no information to disclose. The IPO is expected to proceed within about six months; if completed it would rank among the largest Chinese AI listings to date, following Unitree Robotics' Shanghai STAR Market debut on August 19 and CXMT's blockbuster Shanghai IPO in July.

title: CATL Chairman Warns Compressed EV Launch Schedules Are Producing Battery Batch Failures as China Rolls Out Nearly 3 New Models a Day
detail: CATL Chairman Robin Zeng warned at the 2026 World Power Battery Conference in Yibin, Sichuan Province, on September 3, that China's breakneck pace of new-vehicle launches — more than 600 models introduced in 2026, or roughly three a day — is squeezing battery validation cycles and has already contributed to batch-level quality failures reaching the market. Zeng said CATL maintains an internal 'Opponent Group' with veto authority over shipments and targets a defect rate of one per billion cells, far stricter than industry-standard parts-per-million tolerances, as a check against the compressed timelines automakers are demanding amid the price war. The warning lands as Chinese manufacturers account for more than 70% of global power-battery installation volume, meaning even small defect rates can translate into large absolute numbers of substandard cells entering production — an early crack in the narrative of unqualified Chinese battery dominance that has otherwise underpinned CATL's record market share and EV-export growth this year.

media.caption: CATL Chairman Robin Zeng warned that compressed EV validation cycles have contributed to battery batch failures as China launches nearly three new models a day
